message.content: {"skills": [{"category": "diagnosis", "trigger": "When evaluating a well-circumscribed, smooth or slightly lobulated mediastinal mass on chest radiography to differentiate benign cystic lesions from solid tumors.", "steps": ["Confirm the mass is located in the superior mediastinum and assess its margins for smoothness or slight lobulation, which suggests a benign etiology.", "Examine the lateral view specifically for increased soft-tissue density positioned directly posterior to the tracheal air column; this retrotracheal location is anatomically specific to esophageal origin.", "Distinguish from lymphoma (typically associated with bulky, confluent adenopathy rather than a discrete retrotracheal cyst) and neurogenic tumors (which are characteristically located in the posterior paravertebral gutter rather than immediately behind the trachea)."]}]}
